references.text: Jesus' words that whoever sees Him sees the Father emphasize the same identity between the sent one and the sender as in John 13:20.
Here it is expressed that honor for the Father comes through honoring the Son, reflecting the logic that receiving the sent one is to receive the sender.
The Father has testified about the Son, and whoever receives the Son receives the Father's testimony, a direct parallel to the theology of John 13:20.
Philip asks to see the Father, and Jesus answers that whoever has seen Him has seen the Father, confirming that receiving the Son is receiving the Father.
Jesus prays that the disciples may be one, so that the world may believe that the Father has sent the Son, based on the principle that receiving the sent one is to receive the sender.
John the Baptist points to Jesus as the sent one, and Jesus confirms that whoever receives a prophet receives the reward of a prophet, a direct parallel to John 13:20.
